description:
Astro_X is an independent technology team focused on building innovative software solutions using Artificial Intelligence, data science, and modern web technologies.

Our goal is to transform complex scientific data into accessible, meaningful insights through practical applications that address real-world challenges.

For NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, we are developing FlameInsight AI, an AI-powered platform designed to explore and analyze NASA's microgravity combustion research.
summary: IGNIS-0G is an interactive microgravity combustion and spacecraft fire safety intelligence platform grounded in 17 verified NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) flight experiments (Saffire, FLEX, BASS, ACME, SoFIE, and BRE). Designed to bridge decades of orbital combustion research with next-generation Artemis lunar and Mars mission safety, the platform integrates four core engineering modules: a real-time 60FPS Navier-Stokes and diffusion flame simulator across planetary gravities (1.0g Earth, 0.38g Mars, 0.16g Moon, and 0.0g ISS); a NASA-STD-6001B material flammability and toxicity risk matrix; multi-axis telemetry correlation visualizations; and a zero-hallucination Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) Flight Safety Analyst supporting both offline TF-IDF search and multi-provider LLMs. IGNIS-0G empowers aerospace engineers and mission planners to evaluate cabin fire hazards and suppression trade-offs before flight.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

IGNIS-0G is an interactive microgravity combustion and spacecraft fire safety intelligence platform grounded in 17 verified NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) flight experiments (Saffire, FLEX, BASS, ACME, SoFIE, and BRE). It translates raw orbital fire data into four integrated engineering tools:

1. Real-Time 60FPS Combustion & Aerodynamics Simulator: Approximates Navier-Stokes flow fields, buoyancy forces (Grashof and Froude numbers), and diffusion flame kinetics across four planetary gravity regimes (1.0g Earth, 0.38g Mars, 0.16g Moon, and 0.0g ISS), featuring interactive forced-ventilation airflow (0–20 cm/s), oxygen concentration (15%–36% O2), and cool-flame chemical reaction modes.

2. NASA-STD-6001B Material Flammability Risk Matrix: Evaluates spacecraft cabin materials (Nomex, PMMA acrylic, Kapton wiring, Polyurethane foam, Cellulose, and Kevlar) across mission atmospheres (ISS Nominal, Artemis EVA 34% O2, Orion Launch, and Mars Habitat), comparing flame spread rates, toxic CO offgassing, and Water Mist vs. CO2 suppression trade-offs.

3. Multi-Axis Telemetry Correlation Graphs: Visualizes non-linear relationships between oxygen fraction, forced ventilation velocity, flame temperature, and toxic emissions across NASA flight datasets.

4. Zero-Hallucination RAG Flight Safety Analyst: A hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation assistant combining deterministic offline TF-IDF cosine-similarity search with optional multi-provider LLM synthesis (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, OpenRouter), strictly anchored to verified NASA PSI record citations.

Benefits & Intended Impact

Fire in microgravity behaves counter-intuitively—forming spherical diffusion flames, invisible low-temperature cool flames, and accelerating rapidly in elevated-oxygen exploration cabins like Artemis (34% O2). IGNIS-0G gives spacecraft engineers, safety officers, and mission planners an immediate, accessible pre-flight decision-support environment to test ventilation thresholds, select NASA-STD-6001B compliant materials, and query historical flight evidence without needing supercomputing clusters.

Tools, Languages & Architecture

- Frontend & Physics Engine: React 18, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, HTML5 Canvas (60FPS particle/vector field solver), and Recharts.

- AI & Data Retrieval: Custom client-side TF-IDF vector retrieval engine with strict citation grounding over structured NASA PSI flight records.

- Open-Source Repository: https://github.com/Eyad-Yahia/ignis-0g

- Live Deployment: https://darling-longma-a7d1e1.netlify.app

Creativity & Engineering Considerations

To ensure maximum reliability and zero hallucination in safety-critical engineering queries, IGNIS-0G operates 100% client-side with an offline-first TF-IDF retrieval engine that works even without external API keys, while storing any optional user-supplied LLM keys strictly in volatile session memory (RAM) rather than persistent storage.
